objectives.wording: Compare rheumatic, valvular, ischaemic, hypertrophic and inflammatory disease by epidemiology, inherited risks, mechanisms and course.
Define heart failure and assign stages in representative cases.
Compare left and right failure and distinguish impaired contraction from impaired filling.
Explain neurohormonal responses and ventricular remodelling and their effects over time.
Review simulated cases for ischaemia, arrhythmia, anaemia, thyroid disease, dietary triggers and medicines.

Elicit, document and present a history to establish the diagnosis, cause and severity of heart failure, including presenting complaints, precipitating and aggravating factors, risks, exercise tolerance, sleep changes and features suggestive of infective endocarditis.
Demonstrate and document a targeted examination and estimate severity from the findings.
Prioritize likely and time-critical diagnoses from a simulated presentation.
Counsel a simulated patient on individualized sodium intake, activity and limitations.
Document and present a plan tailored to phenotype, underlying cause and clinical severity.

For an adult with a common form of congenital heart disease, elicit, document and present the history, demonstrate the general examination and relevant findings, and formulate, document and present a management plan.
Trace streptococcal disease to rheumatic fever and valve damage and explain diagnostic criteria, prophylaxis, treatment and complications.
Explain how structural and haemodynamic changes predispose to arrhythmias, especially atrial fibrillation.
Demonstrate assessment of pulse volume, character and variation and relate findings to representative causes.
Measure blood pressure and interpret representative alterations in valve disease, failure and tamponade.
Demonstrate positioning, identification and measurement of jugular venous pressure.
Characterize timing, pitch, quality and radiation and demonstrate relevant dynamic manoeuvres.
Select and interpret ECG, chest radiography and blood cultures when indicated.
Compare indications and representative findings for echocardiography, BNP, exercise testing, nuclear imaging and angiography.
Record a tracing using correct lead placement and interpret representative findings.
Justify the test, record a tracing and interpret representative findings.
Record a 12-lead ECG and interpret findings in a simulated hypertension case.
Assess the severity of valvular heart disease using clinical, laboratory and imaging findings and describe the level of intervention required, including surgery.
Distinguish acute and subacute presentations and integrate echocardiography, cultures and susceptibility findings into a simulated plan.
Demonstrate aseptic collection, labelling and transfer using an approved simulation.
Demonstrate aseptic collection, labelling and transport on a mannequin.
Distinguish plausible bloodstream infection from contamination using sample results and clinical findings.
Discuss pharmacology, indications and contraindications for diuretics, ACE inhibitors, beta blockers, aldosterone antagonists and cardiac glycosides in heart failure.
Match representative indications to valvuloplasty, valvotomy, revascularization or transplantation.
Compare adult presentations of cyanotic and acyanotic defects and explain distinguishing findings.
Explain the procedure and demonstrate safe intramuscular injection on a task trainer.
Interpret representative population patterns and relate antecedents to ischaemic disease risk.
Distinguish modifiable and nonmodifiable risks and prioritize prevention opportunities in sample cases.
Trace lipoprotein handling and explain how dyslipidaemia contributes to plaque formation.
Explain plaque evolution and relate chronic and acute changes to clinical outcomes.

Elicit, document and present a history covering onset, evolution, presenting symptoms, risk factors, family history, comorbidities, complications, medication use and prior atherosclerosis, ischaemic heart disease or coronary syndromes.
Generate, document and present a differential diagnosis, prioritizing diagnoses that must be excluded, likelihood and severity.
Distinguish stable angina, unstable angina and myocardial infarction using representative presentations.
Compare indications and representative findings for echocardiography, stress testing and angiography.
Discuss the pathogenesis, recognition and management of acute coronary syndrome complications, including arrhythmias, shock, left ventricular dysfunction, papillary muscle rupture and pericarditis.
Assess pain and reassess response to appropriate relief in an acute coronary scenario.
Explain indications and safety checks for nitrates, antiplatelets, GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors, beta blockers and ACE inhibitors.
Define representative syndromes and compare their evolution and outcomes.
Identify who needs monitored coronary care and explain supportive measures in a simulated case.
Compare drug roles by presentation and justify selection and safety checks in simulation.
Perform, demonstrate and document a physical examination including vascular and cardiac examination appropriate to the presentation.
Select chest radiography and biomarkers where indicated and interpret findings in relation to symptom timing.
Interpret a sample profile and justify desirable values in the patient's risk context.
Compare indications for thrombolysis, percutaneous intervention and bypass surgery.
Identify eligible patients and explain rehabilitation components and follow-up.
Compare indications, formulations, dosing principles, adverse effects and monitoring using a current reference.
Observe and take an assigned role in a supervised ACLS exercise.
Demonstrate adult BLS on a mannequin.
Agree on feasible cardiovascular risk reduction with a simulated patient using empathetic communication.
Agree on practical targets for weight, alcohol, activity and sodium with a simulated patient.
Distinguish community-acquired, hospital-acquired and aspiration pneumonia.
Predict likely organisms from care setting and host immune status.
Relate pathogenesis to presentation, disease course and complications.
Elicit, document and present a pneumonia history including illness evolution, risk factors, immune status and occupational risks.
Generate, document and present a differential diagnosis and prioritize it based on the clinical presentation.

Order and interpret investigations appropriate to the presentation, including CBC, PA chest radiography, Mantoux testing, sputum Gram stain and culture with susceptibility, pleural fluid examination and culture, HIV testing and arterial blood gases.
Justify when HRCT, viral culture, PCR or other specialized tests could change management.
Use clinical severity and support needs to justify disposition for representative cases.
Explain diagnosis, care, follow-up and warning signs to a simulated patient and family.
Demonstrate and document general and lung examination and assess severity and complications.
Demonstrate arterial blood gas sampling and specimen handling on a mannequin.
Interpret a supplied arterial blood gas and explain its oxygenation, ventilation and acid–base findings.
State the indications for arterial blood gas analysis and interpret supplied ABG results, identifying the primary disturbance and the degree of compensation.
Demonstrate preparation, aspiration and safety checks on a mannequin.
Select fluid tests and interpret a sample report in clinical context.
Select and write a simulated empiric prescription using likely pathogens, spectrum and patient factors.

In a simulated case, select and prescribe an appropriate empirical antimicrobial, describing the choice in terms of its pharmacology and antimicrobial spectrum, and revise the prescription when culture and sensitivity results are supplied.
Explain when isolation and barrier precautions are indicated based on suspected transmission.
Explain supportive care, oxygen monitoring and indications for ventilatory escalation.
Use current applicable guidance to identify indications for both vaccines.
Explain benefits, expected reactions and follow-up using teach-back in simulation.
Explain how immunity, age, malignancy, neutropenia, HIV, travel and comorbidity can modify fever.
Distinguish altered hypothalamic set point from excess heat accumulation using examples.
Compare representative causes across Indian regions using season, exposures and local epidemiology.
Link inflammatory mechanisms to representative clinical patterns.
Explain representative mechanisms and clues to haematological and lymphatic malignancies.

Elicit, document and present a fever history including evolution, pattern, associated symptoms, immune status, comorbidities, risk factors, occupational, travel and environmental exposures, and medication use.
Perform a systematic examination to establish diagnosis and severity, including general, skin, mucosal, lymph node, chest and abdominal examination with assessment of the liver and spleen.
Prioritize infective, inflammatory, malignant and rheumatological causes from a simulated case.

Order and interpret investigations based on the fever differential, including CBC with differential, peripheral smear, urinalysis with sediment, chest radiography and other imaging, blood and urine cultures, sputum Gram stain and culture, sputum AFB testing and culture, CSF analysis, pleural and other body fluid analysis, routine stool examination and culture, serology, FNAC, biopsy, bone marrow examination and QBC.
Match imaging modalities to suspected sites and causes of fever.
Justify a provisional plan based on acuity and immune status and specify when to revise it.
Build a staged assessment using acuity, exposure, duration and localizing findings.
Relate dysregulated host responses to organ dysfunction and representative manifestations.
Discuss the pathophysiology, clinical features and management of heat cramps, heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Discuss the pathophysiology, causes and clinical manifestations of fever of unknown origin in immunocompetent patients, neutropenic patients, hospitalized patients and people with HIV.
For prolonged fever, explain indications and expected findings for inflammatory and rheumatologic tests, pathogen serology including HIV, and bone marrow aspiration and biopsy.
Present a prioritized, cost-conscious diagnostic plan based on clinical clues.
Explain the working diagnosis, uncertainties and treatment to a simulated patient and family.
Observe and demonstrate an assigned assistance role for marrow aspiration and biopsy in simulation.
Explain indications for aspiration and biopsy and interpret representative results.
Explain indications for aspiration and biopsy and interpret representative results.
Interpret measured induration using the exposure history and immune status and explain test limitations.
Trace bilirubin production, conjugation and excretion and explain abnormal patterns.
Compare major causes of liver injury and explain their mechanisms.
Elicit and present symptoms, exposures, medicines, sexual and vaccination history and family history.
Demonstrate and document a focused examination for jaundice, chronic liver disease and decompensation.
Prioritize likely causes of a simulated presentation using clinical clues.
Select and interpret blood counts, bilirubin, liver tests, hepatitis serology and ascitic fluid results.
Compare management priorities for hepatitis, cirrhosis and its major complications, including portal hypertensive bleeding and liver cancer.
Compare transmission, virology, immune injury and clinical course across hepatitis viruses.
Identify indications and precautions and explain expected benefits to a simulated patient.
Trace progression from steatosis to hepatitis and cirrhosis and explain clinical evolution.
Explain the causes, features, complications and management of cirrhosis.
Explain the causes, features, complications and management of portal hypertension.
Classify representative agents and explain mechanisms and injury patterns.
Explain stone formation, inflammation, clinical course and complications.
Compare indications and representative findings for ultrasound, MRCP and ERCP.
Use bilirubin fractions, liver test patterns and hepatitis serology to narrow the differential.
Demonstrate a supervised or simulated assistance role and interpret a supplied fluid panel.
Identify representative indications for transplant evaluation.
Recognize representative seroconversion findings and distinguish common mimics.
Apply the applicable CDC classification to supplied clinical and laboratory data.
Recognize common lesions and explain their mechanisms and evolution.
Elicit and document exposures, STI history, opportunistic infection risks and nutritional status respectfully.
Prioritize likely causes of a presenting symptom using the clinical setting and immune status.
Select and interpret appropriate diagnostic tests and classify severity from a simulated case.
Demonstrate nonjudgmental counselling on transmission prevention and verify understanding.
Explain diagnosis, treatment and follow-up in a simulated consultation.
Demonstrate respectful, inclusive communication without assumptions about identity or behaviour.
Relate CD4 count to representative infection risks and explain how it informs assessment.
Compare mechanisms, course and findings of common opportunistic infections.

In a supplied HIV/opportunistic-infection scenario, choose and interpret the indicated CBC, sputum examination and culture, blood culture, stool analysis, CSF analysis and chest radiograph findings in an OSCE or viva setting.
Compare indications and representative findings for chest CT, brain CT and brain MRI.
Explain when to use pulse oximetry, arterial blood gases and chest radiography and interpret sample findings.
Match preventive medicines to representative infection risks and applicable indications.
Compare representative cancers by pathogenesis, course and presentation.
Compare indications and adverse effects of representative therapies by likely cause.
Explain the principles of combination antiretroviral treatment and compare antiretroviral classes, their main effects, adverse reactions and interactions in a supplied HIV/AIDS scenario.
Explore barriers and agree on a feasible medication adherence plan.
Discuss the pathogenesis of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) and describe its management.
Explain the principles of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis and describe the regimens used, applying them to a hypothetical exposure scenario.
Apply relevant ethical and legal guidance to a simulated disclosure decision.
Connect genetic susceptibility and loss of tolerance to representative autoimmune diseases.
Classify causes by inflammatory, mechanical, infectious and other mechanisms.
Build a staged approach using localization, timing and underlying mechanism.
Use acute, subacute and chronic patterns to narrow the differential.
Distinguish arthralgia from arthritis, articular from periarticular symptoms and mechanical from inflammatory patterns.
Match common symptoms and examination findings to articular or periarticular disease.
Elicit, document and present a history that helps distinguish the possible causes of the presenting joint condition.
Perform a systematic examination of all joints, muscles and skin to establish diagnosis and severity.
Prioritize causes based on a simulated history and examination.
Explain the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up to a simulated patient.
Elicit preferences and incorporate them into a simulated treatment decision.
Explore effects on daily life, work and family in a simulated encounter.
Identify cases requiring specialist consultation and justify urgency.
Identify extra-articular manifestations and explain their diagnostic implications.
Select, prescribe and communicate treatment options for systemic rheumatologic conditions.
Describe the workup for the presumed cause and explain the indications for and interpretation of CBC, anti-CCP, RA, ANA, DNA and other autoimmunity tests.
Identify diagnostic and therapeutic indications in representative scenarios.
Enumerate indications for plain radiographs of joints and interpret the findings.
Develop a plan based on disease activity, organ involvement and patient factors.
Compare the rationale for conventional and biologic disease-modifying therapy.
Set monitoring and follow-up goals and explain them using teach-back.
Explain the evaluation and management of joint pain due to gout and other crystal arthropathies.
Compare prevalence, genetic susceptibility and causes of primary and secondary hypertension.
Explain how vascular resistance, volume and neurohormonal regulation contribute to sustained pressure elevation.
Define and classify hypertension.
Compare typical patterns and identify clues to a secondary cause.
Match representative findings to renal, endocrine, vascular and medication-related causes.
Recognize cardiac, renal, retinal, neurological and vascular complications.

Elicit, document and present a history covering blood pressure duration and levels, symptoms, comorbidities, lifestyle, risks, family history, psychosocial and environmental factors, diet, and previous and concurrent therapy.
Use representative findings to prioritize primary and secondary causes.
